text: Hadrun, spring 1423: I traded blows with the roc until it fled. Berov and Radanya were already dead. I took their boy home. Small Tusk.
1453: Ivoard Hask brought me the coal in the old Velun reliquary. I knew Yaga-Shura's heart the moment I saw it, and I set it anyway. The warmth has been in me since.
This Highharvestide, Small Tusk asked me straight whether I made the crown. I told him: the band, the setting, and the warmth that began then. I did not tell him whose heart it is.
I told him fire, hammer and pyre cannot break the coal; only a giant's forge fed with a giant's own blood. Mine. I did not tell him the rest of the price.
At the almshouse dead-house I broke the ramp door. The smell of hot iron lit something in me. I hope the boy didn't see it.
I asked that the ash wafers be kept out of my reach. I don't know where he hid them, and I don't want to.
Halda refused to open the Saltgate for Lorard's engines, even for me. I told Small Tusk forcing the gate means war, and that the roc grew worse once the coal was loose.
Over the Great Pyre the Gallowsbird had him. He was dying. I quenched him in my blood. He lives, and he is Banked now, touched like all of them. He doesn't know what I poured into him.
